known.title: Doctor skips repairable SDKs when their standalone CLI is absent

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a both-tools repo selects Codex workers from a Claude session, but the Codex SDK and standalone Codex CLI are absent.
The new programs["codex"] condition suppresses both the missing-SDK row and its --fix installer. However, worker.py:164-184 still routes this work through the Codex kit and refuses its missing SDK with instructions to run doctor --fix. The SDK supplies its own executable (codex.py:38-47), so doctor could install the required dependency without a standalone CLI. Following the prescribed recovery command now leaves the worker blocked. The equivalent programs["claude"] condition at doctor.py:359 has the same problem for Claude kits; tests/test_tools_agent_sdk.py:102-108 explicitly exercises SDK reads without the standalone Claude CLI. Determine SDK repair eligibility from reachable kit runs rather than requiring the standalone executable.
